from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 5  # sources
    J = 8  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [160, 182, 147, 195, 139]
    demands = [46, 12, 38, 37, 13, 36, 27, 24]
    cost_matrix = [[19.38, 20.58, 3.87, 28.91, 4.25, 19.07, 21.14, 29.41], [27.01, 8.04, 28.29, 24.66, 3.91, 24.84, 19.63, 24.83], [29.46, 5.04, 28.39, 26.72, 11.69, 11.79, 8.06, 10.44], [3.73, 25.28, 12.97, 21.51, 28.23, 22.13, 11.48, 5.98], [6.09, 25.81, 24.62, 14.9, 6.06, 21.86, 10.56, 21.13]]
    emission_matrix = [[13.57, 9.21, 3.11, 7.96, 6.16, 4.65, 15.03, 1.0], [12.34, 12.83, 9.16, 10.7, 4.06, 1.31, 4.38, 4.97], [9.43, 17.47, 13.5, 5.43, 3.06, 6.83, 16.05, 7.11], [20.0, 9.15, 7.88, 12.8, 8.81, 6.31, 7.76, 17.77], [11.17, 14.63, 5.72, 13.76, 16.18, 8.07, 12.72, 16.91]]
    fixed_costs = [[169, 230, 67, 178, 220, 232, 219, 248], [83, 291, 91, 263, 110, 118, 282, 173], [264, 164, 185, 214, 107, 265, 127, 291], [181, 59, 256, 139, 286, 266, 293, 273], [54, 92, 146, 96, 202, 219, 186, 258]]
    moq = [[10, 13, 15, 5, 19, 5, 10, 6], [8, 20, 13, 6, 20, 7, 16, 20], [15, 11, 7, 10, 6, 6, 14, 13], [5, 10, 10, 9, 14, 19, 6, 13], [11, 7, 9, 10, 8, 12, 17, 14]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Supply Chain Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: [As of this memo]
Subject: Balancing shipping cost and carbon impacts across our warehouse-to-store network

Context
Our shipping decisions shape both our cost base and our carbon footprint. We move products from multiple warehouses to multiple stores, and every route has two critical metrics: a per‑unit dollar cost and a per‑unit CO2 emission rate. In practice, the least expensive routes often have higher emissions, while cleaner routes can be more expensive. We need a plan that balances cost discipline with our sustainability commitments, without compromising service.

Operational rules we must respect
- Route activation and setup costs: Each warehouse‑to‑store route requires a one‑time setup charge to initiate service (e.g., contract fees, paperwork, dock preparation). A route is either active or inactive. If we choose to use a route at all, the setup cost is incurred regardless of the eventual shipment volume.
- Minimum order quantities on active routes: Once a route is activated, we must ship at least a predefined minimum on that lane to justify the logistics overhead. Partial truckloads below this threshold are not accepted.
- Supplier limits per store: To align with receiving capacity and vendor management practices, each store may receive deliveries from no more than an allowed number of warehouses.

Supply and demand coverage
- Shipments from each warehouse cannot exceed available inventory.
- Each store must receive at least its required demand to avoid lost sales and service erosion.

Management priority
Leadership has set relative importance for cost and emissions. Our analysis will blend per‑unit shipping costs and per‑unit emissions according to these weights. One‑time route setup costs will be added in full on any activated route; only the per‑unit shipping costs and per‑unit emissions are blended using the management weights.

Business goal
Identify which routes to activate and how much to ship on each active route so that:
- We respect warehouse inventory limits and fulfill each store’s demand.
- Any activated route moves at least its minimum required volume.
- Each store is served by no more than the allowed number of supplying warehouses.
- The resulting blended total—combining weighted variable shipping costs, weighted total emissions, and full route setup costs—achieves the lowest overall value under these priorities and rules.

How we will proceed
- Confirm inputs: warehouse supplies, store demands, per‑route costs and emissions, route setup charges, route minimums, and the per‑store supplier cap.
- Evaluate trade‑offs: compare lower‑cost/higher‑emission lanes with cleaner alternatives, accounting for the effect of route minimums and supplier limits on feasible flow patterns.
- Recommend a shipping plan: a clear set of active routes and shipment quantities that meet service needs and deliver the best blended outcome.
- Monitor and adjust: revisit the plan as demand, inventory positions, carrier availability, and emissions factors evolve.
